title: ork retry re-lands a committed run whose landing was blocked
findings_note: 2026-11-17: S387 (run ork-20261117-021246-a004) committed, then its landing re-check went red because main's adj records were uncommitted (orchestrator error, fixed in 037800d8). landBlocked (internal/engine/land.go:262-266) stopped the run after its one land fix; NotResumable (internal/engine/resume.go:24-25) refuses retry for any committed run, so the orchestrator merged main, re-ran the checks and fast-forwarded main by hand (dae60175). Owner rule 2026-11-17: deterministic work runs as code.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
2026-11-17: S387 committed, then its landing re-check went red after merging main (main's `adj lint` failed on uncommitted supersede edits, fixed in 037800d8). It had already used its one land fix round, so `landBlocked` stopped it (`internal/engine/land.go:262-266`). `ork retry` then refused it: `NotResumable` returns "committed its slice; there is nothing to resume" for any record with a commit (`internal/engine/resume.go:24-25`), and the daemon refuses the same way (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1496`). The orchestrator had to merge main into the worktree, render, run the checks and fast-forward main by hand. Owner rule (2026-11-17): regular, deterministic steps are code.

Owner decisions (2026-11-17): `ork retry RUN` on such a run re-enters landing and resets the land fix count, so a red re-check gets one more implementer fix round before it stops again [land.retry-relands, adj 458]. Only a committed run that stopped in the land stage, with its worktree and branch still there, qualifies; any other committed run keeps today's refusal [land.retry-scope, adj 459].

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/engine/resume.go:20-32` (`NotResumable`: allow committed + stopped_from land)
- `internal/engine/resume.go:101-156` (`resumeStopped`: re-enter `land`, reset `LandFixes`)
- `internal/engine/land.go:258-276` (`landBlocked`: unchanged rule, one fix round per retry)
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:1488-1500` (retry refusal path)
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:1296` and `:1541` (other `NotResumable` callers: a re-landable run is not resumed by `ork run`)
- `internal/engine/resume_test.go`
- `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`
- `docs/guide.md` (ork retry)
- `docs/design.md` (landing blocked; retry)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestRetryRelandsACommittedRunStoppedAtLand` in `internal/engine/resume_test.go`: a record in state stopped, `stopped_from` land, a commit, `land_fixes` 1, worktree and branch present; `ork retry` puts it in state land with `land_fixes` 0, and with a green re-check the branch lands and the record ends landed.
- `TestRetryRelandGetsOneFixRound` in `internal/engine/resume_test.go`: same record, the re-check is red; the run gets one implementer fix round (feedback kind land), and if the re-check is red again it stops with "land blocked".
- `TestRetryStillRefusesOtherCommittedRuns` in `internal/engine/resume_test.go`: a committed run stopped from any state but land, or with a missing worktree or branch, is refused with today's message or one naming what is missing.
- `TestDaemonRetryRelandsCommittedRun` in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: the daemon's retry of such a run is accepted (no CodeRefused) and the run returns to land.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests above and see them red for the stated reason.
2. `NotResumable`: return "" for a stopped record with a commit and `StoppedFrom == runrec.StateLand`; keep the refusal for every other committed record.
3. `resumeStopped`: for such a record, check the worktree and branch exist (refuse naming the missing one), reject `--rounds` with a refusal that says landing gets one fix round, set `LandFixes = 0`, `LandRecheck = true`, clear the stop fields as today, and set the state to land. Do not reset the round limit or rerun implement or checks before landing.
4. `ork run ITEM` and `ork wave start` do not pick up a re-landable run as a resume (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1296`, `:1541`); only `ork retry RUN` re-lands it. Keep their current behaviour for that record.
5. The stop reason "land blocked: ..." names the next step: `ork retry RUN` re-lands with one more fix round.
6. Docs: `docs/guide.md` ork retry entry and `docs/design.md` landing section, citing adj 458 and 459. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet at the end of `## Unreleased`, written by hand.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- ork retry on a committed run stopped in land merges main again, reruns the landing checks and lands when they are green.
- A red re-check after that retry gets exactly one implementer fix round, then stops with land blocked if still red.
- ork retry on any other committed run, or one whose worktree or branch is gone, is refused with a message that says why.
- ork retry --rounds N on a re-landable run is refused with a message that names the one fix round.
- ork run ITEM does not resume a re-landable run.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/engine -run TestRetryRelandsACommittedRunStoppedAtLand -v`
- `go test ./internal/engine -run TestRetryRelandGetsOneFixRound -v`
- `go test ./internal/engine -run TestRetryStillRefusesOtherCommittedRuns -v`
- `go test ./internal/daemon -run TestDaemonRetryRelandsCommittedRun -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` must print nothing.

sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, message "S408: ork retry re-lands a committed run stopped at land".
